Feb 7, 2020Full Date

I will quote directly from the Rulebook:
"Whenever your Character is in a Room with any uncarried Eggs (not carried by any Character), you can try to destroy these Eggs. Resolve this Action as a Shoot Action or Melee Attack Action. Each Injury (of any type) destroys 1 Egg.
In the case of a Melee Attack Action, the Character does not draw a Contamination card or suffer Wounds if they miss.
You can also throw grenades into a Room with uncarried Eggs as if an Intruder were there. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs, a Molotov Cocktail destroys 1 Egg.
After every single attempt to destroy an Egg, you must perform a Noise roll."
Based on the aforementioned underlined, I can conclude that:
- Each Melee/Shot Action, destroys 1 egg if at least 1 injury of any king is caused.
- No Contamination if you miss
- Noise roll after every single attempt.

Jakub Stefański

Image: Poland flag

I think that @Marko learned that you get contamination cards after melee attacks in general, not from attacking eggs.

Each Injury (of any type) destroys 1 Egg.

Yannos Smith @Hallequin

Each Melee/Shot Action, destroys 1 egg if at least 1 injury of any king is caused.

I don't think that "each" means the same as "at least 1". You may roll double hits or in other ways inflict more injuries with one attack.

For those looking for a slightly longer and more puzzly way to play Wingspan Pocket, I propose
The Bird Lady Variant.
- Same rules as written, in that you first choose one of the 3 actions on your nest, then execute the brown bird powers of your flock... but...
- Instead of your flock consisting of a row of up to 6 birds, with the game ending the round that a player plays their 6th bird, the birds are instead placed in a 3x3 grid (similar to your personal tableau in Castle Combo). The game ends the round that a player plays their 9th bird to complete their 3x3 grid.

I would assume this means that the swapping bodies thing functions something like a biological version of Star Trek transporters.
